A cooperative flying club

Learn more. Fly more. Do it together.

Members help record operations, launch sailplanes, maintain equipment and facilities, and—when qualified—serve as tow pilots or instructors. In return, club instructors volunteer their time, keeping training accessible.

Membership, fees, and acceptance remain subject to club approval and current policies. Published fees below reproduce the existing club schedule and should be confirmed before payment.

No experience needed

New members can begin at the very start and progress with certificated volunteer instructors.

Instruction included

You pay aircraft operating costs; club instructors do not charge separately for their time.

Everyone contributes

Field operations are part of the experience—not a chore bolted onto it.

Young aviators

Start early. Build real skills.

Students can begin learning before they are old enough to solo. FAA rules permit solo glider flight at 14. The club’s junior program is space-available and expects regular participation in Saturday operations.

Student membership offers reduced fees for qualifying members under 24. Junior members learn by helping on the field as well as flying.

Try the controls

Three instructional flights. $250.

An introductory membership lets prospective members experience club operations and fly with an instructor.
